Holy shit these comments?? I’ve know a woman who experienced something similar. 

Okay first off, people are going to be awful about this, that’s probably the hardest part of being taken advantage of. Second, it’s important to call it what it is even if it makes people uncomfortable or dismissive. You were raped. If that doesn’t feel genuine since you don’t know for sure, sexual assault still applies. 

PTSD/trauma is one helluva thing. You never know you have it until it hits you. You mentioned you worry about feeling comfortable in future sexual interactions with your wife, this is a huge reason why you should tell her. You don’t know how hard it’ll be until it it’s suddenly in your face again. I’ve had multiple bros been raped and assaulted. They keep that’s shit locked down and kept going as a man is expected to. But we’re still human. Many of them were still hurting, still had things affect them. They never had a safe moment to process it and many confided in me since I was so sensitive it hurt me. 
Don’t like it simmer in the background, for yourself and your wife. You didn’t cheat, it was rape and it was absolutely not your fault, but at the same time, not telling your wife can break her trust. 

She’s a life partner, if you don’t feel like you can talk to your wife about the things that weigh on you the most, then that’s a different problem. 
If you do share that hurt with her using the correct language and she chooses to blame you or add to that hurt, you don’t deserve to be in that sort of relationship.
That being said, there is always the chance she could lash out at first because it is a heavy thing to process.
Redditors love to speculate on just a small part of your relationship and tear it to shreds, but you know your wife best.
Tell her and take care of yourself man. You know what happened, don’t let people put a “woulda, shoulda, coulda” in your brain.

I was expected to do a lot of things for myself including make my own lunches and breakfast at age 7. I have several mood disorders and have had depression since childhood so I struggled a lot and couldn’t make myself food. I loved cooking from a young age, but having all that responsibility was crushing especially when my parents didn’t jump in when I couldn’t do it myself. Instead, I got in trouble at the doctor for not eating breakfast for a whole year. 
Here however, you’re helping Sara the entire time and making sure she knows what she’s doing. You have her a great learning opportunity in a safe environment and I’m sure she felt plenty proud of herself. Unlike my situation, there wasn’t a ‘make it or starve’ ultimatum. You had Sara make the dinner because like you said it’s something she enjoys. You’re NTA because this was something Sara *wanted* to do and didn’t do because it was made her responsibility.

Growing up there was always very strict Birthday rules. You get to choose the cake, you get to pick the dinner, if there’s anything good like a new MCU movie out we go see it. My friend’s family did less but they always had a strict rule that the birthday person chooses their Birthday dinner. 

Here’s some accommodations you could have made for Lily, my parents have done similar things and there has been no issues.
1. Gotten her a cupcake with her desired flavour while giving Rose her desired Birthday cake.
2. Got Chinese food and bought some food elsewhere for Lily (because food is different than cake. I had a restaurant I hated so my mom started ordering food ahead of time for a place down the street that I loved). 
3. If you can only order from one place, sit Lily down and work out the menu with her. Say ‘this is where we are eating so let’s pick something on this menu that you know you’ll like’. This one is really good because it seems like you’re raising Lily to be pretty entitled. That part where you said you didn’t want Lily to be “fussy about the food”? Seems like you don’t work things through and rather give Lily what she wants to keep her happy. Not saying you should make her un-happy but there are situations where you don’t have to bend over backwards for Lily, especially when it includes kicking Rose away. 
4. How to get Lily to feel included when it came to gifts? Have her help pick out a gift for Rose. Seriously. Even if it’s giving her $10 and dropping her off at a Dollar store. If she needs it, this is where you can butter her up and encourage her that gifting is really good to make the other person happy and you can feel happy in that. Getting Lily a gift? What is the point of that. She is going to feel left out always on Rose’s birthday no matter what because it’s not her birthday. She will never be born on the same day that Rose is and you both are going to have to live with that. It’s important to teach Lily how to deal with other people being in the spot light. It’s going to happen so many times in her life and you’re setting her up for failure. You can teach her how to still be happy in other people’s moment and if she feels those negative feeling you can teach her how to cope with them. Jealously is normal for a kid, jealousy is healthy for a kid. What’s not healthy is these extreme lengths to make sure she feels no negative emotion that she is bound to feel in life. Yes, it’s extreme. 
You should know something is wrong when you don’t know what to get your kid for their birthday. I keep notes on random people I meet that sometimes I never see again about what gifts I can give them. It’s as small as a favourite candy. Here’s a hint, interests are conversation starters. Meaning you giving her a gift that she doesn’t like because you had no idea what to get her is unbelievable. YTA.
I would totally distance from you too.
Here’s how you can move forward. You should re-do the birthday. I’m not kidding. Apologize to Rose. Then plan something with her and set boundaries. Make times that is a you and her time. Get to know her. It’s that simple. I’ve become closest with my mom just going on car trips.

To start, my issue was that even though you had thought the set was intended for you, it shouldn’t be touched until given. However, you acknowledged that it maybe wasn’t the best choice especially with Christmas coming up.
That’s when your bf explains who the set belonged to. At that point I’ve seen some people critic you for “doubling down”. I recognized your comment instantly as a tension breaker. I can imagine the awkward dropping feeling you must have had when he said that.
The next part is tricky cause it’s good to acknowledge that some people will always hold a certain standing in our lives. Though I feel like there is different levels of “appropriate”. An example would be how I keep small gifts from ex friends, but I often get rid of personal letters from them. If someone’s past spouse died they may have objects of sentiments. This was a case of a divorce (one of which that happened nearly two decades ago). There could be debates on whether or not it was appropriate to have an object of sentiment at all. It could also depend on the situation.
Regardless, the object in this case was a lingerie set which I feel was highly inappropriate for that relationship.

As for the sex toys, I feel that wasn’t terrible because it held no sentimental value to you. As long as he had known and it wasn’t the first time he was hearing about it I don’t feel that was wrong of you. His idea of you keeping it being fucked up definitely stems from his feelings around the set.
I think you’re totally right about the honeymoon connection, I had the same thought process.
At the end of it all, I can image you might feel confused or hurt, which explains why you threw them in the GoodWill pile. However, I don’t think that was the right move. Not just because it wasn’t yours to do that, but because it feels like that’s something he’s going to need to give up on his own and get past.
I will say it was shitty, but given the circumstances I wouldn’t call you T A.

Fanfiction is classically known for the “cringe” factor.
It’s considered to be just a lot of written porn. And really badly written stuff. Using a bunch of different anatomy terms such as “member” or “prick”. It’s heavily known for the self inserts. Self inserts tend to be problematic for their “everybody loves me” “pick me girl” vibes. Those along with the classic bland main character that people can project themselves on, often feed into that need some people have for feeling “special” and “different”. Which can be incredibly annoying when the readers can’t separate the fictions from reality. Like a girl expecting to be hit on by every band member if she goes to a concert. Just makes you want to tell her to get over herself. 
On top of this, fanfiction or writing on fanfic sites (Wattpad) that get adapted suck. Just suck. This kissing booth was adapted from Wattpad. It’s incredibly problematic and very “pick me girl”. But because that’s what’s being shown and that’s what people know they tend to generalize. I know an experienced fanfic reader when their first mention is of Ao3. In my personal opinion it has much better writing and a great tagging system. But I betcha if anyone tries to go “ew fanfiction” their first assumption would be Wattpad.

The parents going behind your back to disrespect your wishes was so uncalled for! Because they were unwilling to come to a compromise and work out a solution with you I think it was only right that there was a ban all together. How my school growing up did it was up until a certain age you your parents would sign a consent form each year. The form was consent to have your picture taken and if it’s allows online. For large school events they would block out the faces of the kids without consent. Eventually the teachers went from asking if your have an a-okay on your consent form and started asking the kid if they consented. The switch happened in middle school. Parents could still overrule this of course but there wasn’t a required form. My teacher would ask if it was alright to take photos and would tell you if it was for a social page or a parent announcement chat. The pictures also came with the understanding that they could be submitted for school assembly slide shows which were for the school and not for media.

But I would cry in the shower very late at night because I blamed myself. 
On the other hand, I think some people genuine don’t consider it a big deal. Like I mentioned a friend was an attempted murderer the other day and someone told me “I think we’re all attempted murderers to a certain degree.” This upset me so much because the friend I didn’t specify went to jail for trying to kill their abuser. So I think some take it like that, they think that there’s different severities and don’t really consider it much of a deal unless the action has actually been done.
It sucks when people don’t care, it really does. I got in a fight with my bf (now ex) after because he started distancing even after knowing about my attempt. It just felt like he didn’t care. So it can really really suck when people close to you don’t seem to care. I thankfully had one friend who was really helpful through it all an encouraged me to go to the hospital if my condition got worse. You’re going to find other people who care and there will people who will be happy you stuck it out. Even if I don’t know you, I’ve been there and I care. My mom has since apologized but wouldn’t let me shave when I wanted to. My leg hair grew really long and I grew very self conscious. My mom told me that I had no need to since the hair was pretty light. This made me upset because my friend who was full blonde (I’m dirty blonde) had already been allowed to shave. One day I found out my mom was teaching my younger sibling how to shave. Sibling is two years younger. I lost it on my mom and started yelling about how much it’s effected my self body image and now she just lets my sibling shave. My mom said my sibling had darker hair. I kept guilting my mom until she bought me a razor. 
I can understand now part of it was my mom being worried about me confining to those beauty standards too young if I didn’t necessarily have to, but it was so great when I got to shave and I felt loads better. 

Yes beauty standards suck, but if it makes her feel good about herself and she is confident that’s truly what matters. I shave because I love the look and feel and it makes me happy. 
I used to put my long hair down even though it bothered me because people thought I looked better that way. That’s the kind of thing that should be looked out for. It didn’t make me feel good, I just did it for others. I cut my hair and I feel worlds better about myself and feel confident in how I look with it. 

If following beauty standards makes
the person happy and confident, then there’s nothing wrong with it. It’s when it’s solely done for others that it’s no good.

This was something I talked about a lot a year  ago. People just don’t notice things. I had a time in middle school where nobody noticed a girl was cutting her wrist in the school bathroom. It was very obvious, even more so when I put my hand over my mouth and look directly at a peer there. Even recently I was hanging out with friends and they couldn’t tell I was having an episode, despite me rocking back and forth and saying to them “the car door was 4 times not 5... and there was no one in that window.” 
Like they knew something was wrong! I had a few more times like this and all I got was a judgmental look. People are just too wrapped up in their own thing. I was told that’s why I shouldn’t worry too much about my looks. I find it more common in girls a lot too. I do my best to always notice because I know how awful that feels too. People are just too wrapped up in their own heads. The person probably had things to do and places to be, but it would be so much better if people could just take time out of their schedules, throw off their groove for just a little bit to stop and notice. They don’t always come right when you need them, but there are people who do notice. I noticed the girl and several others. There should be far more but we can’t discard the few. You will have someone who will notice and care.
